spectral_response: Diseased leaves reflect more in the visible (up to +15% near 690 nm: chlorophyll loss) and in the SWIR water bands (+14% at ~1450 nm, +19% near 2010 nm: water loss). NIR reflectance is only slightly lower (min -0.019 at 760 nm), consistent with white pustules offsetting the loss of mesophyll scattering (Zhang et al., 2012).
by_date: The healthy-diseased spectral angle grows from 0.96° on 11 Feb to 3.58° on 03 Mar, tracking epidemic development. Early (vegetative) differences are small and mainly in the SWIR, so date-specific effects must be handled by the pooled model.
regions: FDR-significant regions (plot-date means): 580-710 nm (D>H, |d| 0.98 at 650 nm); 1390-1560 nm (D>H, |d| 0.68 at 1420 nm); 1840-2400 nm (D>H, |d| 0.86 at 1890 nm). The NIR plateau is not significant in reflectance, but its first derivative (850-870 nm) is the strongest VNIR feature (J-M peak), matching the NIR-slope signature of mesophyll collapse reported by Tian et al. (2021). The largest derivative J-M is at 1820 nm.
rededge: The red edge shifts to shorter wavelengths in diseased leaves: REP 715.7 -> 714.5 nm (p < 0.001); REV and SDr decrease (p = 0.039, 0.016). Blue shift + lower red-edge amplitude = chlorophyll loss, as for rice blast (Mandal et al., 2022).
pca: PC1 (55.8%) and PC2 (30.2%) are driven by date (η² 0.70, 0.49) and stage, not disease (η² ≤ 0.07). Unsupervised methods cannot separate classes, so supervised feature selection is needed.
permanova: Date explains 31.2% of spectral variance; disease 1.1% (pseudo-F 15.3, p = 0.001) plus 1.6% disease x date. Variety is not significant (p = 0.18). H2 is supported: the disease effect is small but robust.
vi: The best published index reaches AUC 0.668 (PSSRb). Many chlorophyll indices (NDVI, SR, MTCI) show no difference on 11 Feb and change sign; date-consistent indices are mainly water, anthocyanin and disease indices (WI, HI, RVSI, ARI2, SR).
mwri: MWRI = (R1810 - R1830) / (R1810 + R1830): mean |d| 1.49 (min 1.32 on any date), AUC 0.869 vs 0.668 for the best published index. The pair lies on the shoulder of the 1940-nm water band inside one detector (artefact checked: same AUC without splice correction). A second family, ND(R870, R890), captures the NIR slope (AUC 0.774).
cwt: The most sensitive wavelet coefficients are at 1810 nm (fine scales, |d| up to 1.45), 680 nm (chlorophyll well), 1920-1930 nm (water) and 1010 nm at scale 6 (NIR shape). Fine scales capture narrow slope changes; coarse scales capture broad shape (Cheng et al., 2011). Wavelet maxima exceed those of single bands (|d| < 1), consistent with Lv et al. (2023).
